st.3: Banawali, in Rajasthan, shows pre-, mature and post-Harappan phases.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Banawali is in Haryana (Fatehabad district), not Rajasthan. Statement 4 is wrong: Chanhudaro, the bead-making town, had no fortified citadel.

st.2: There is no proof of a rigid caste system; caste became fixed in the Rigvedic (Early Vedic) period.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: uniform bricks show standardisation, not differences of status. Statement 2 is wrong: there is no proof of a rigid caste system in the Harappan age, and caste became fixed only in the Later Vedic period, not the Rigvedic period.

st.2: Hiuen Tsang's Fo-Kuo-Ki states that the Sriparvata vihara lacked patrons.
st.1: Hiuen Tsang visited India during the reigns of both Harsha and Chandragupta II.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Hiuen Tsang came during the reigns of Harsha and Pulakeshin II; Chandragupta II's reign saw Fa-Hien. Statement 2 is wrong: Hiuen Tsang's account is the Si-Yu-Ki; the Fo-Kuo-Ki is Fa-Hien's. Statement 4 is wrong: Fa-Hien visited during the reign of Chandragupta II, not Harsha.

st.2: Madhya Desh lay between the Himalayas and the Vindhyas.

x: All three statements are correct: Brahmarshi Desh was the Ganga–Yamuna Doab and adjoining area, Madhya Desh lay between the Himalayas and the Vindhyas, and in the Later Vedic period the core shifted east to the Doab.

st.2: The Vis (clan) was headed by the Vishpati.

x: All three statements are correct: Jana occurs about 275 times in the Rigveda, the Vis was headed by the Vishpati (the Gramani headed the Grama), and the term janapada does not occur in the Rigveda.

st.3: The Prasthanatrayi consists of the Upanishads, the Brahma Sutra and the Bhagavad Gita.

x: All three statements are correct: about 13 of the 108 Upanishads are principal, they are anti-ritualistic and teach the identity of Atman and Brahman, and the Prasthanatrayi is the Upanishads, the Brahma Sutra and the Bhagavad Gita.

st.3: Samkhya, regarded as the oldest of the six darshanas, was founded by Gautama.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Samkhya is paired with Yoga, while Nyaya is paired with Vaisheshika. Statement 3 is wrong: Samkhya was founded by Kapila; Gautama founded Nyaya.

st.4: Death
st.1: Disease

x: Ushas is the goddess of dawn, Yama the god of death, Rudra the god of disease (and storms) and Aditi the mother of the gods: A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2.

st.1: It is a Jain doctrine holding that every phenomenon arises from a cause.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Pratityasamutpada (dependent origination) is a Buddhist doctrine, not a Jain one. Statement 2 is wrong: the chain has twelve links (nidanas), not ten.

st.1: He was the Buddha's companion for about six years.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Gosala was Mahavira's companion for about six years, not the Buddha's. Statement 3 is wrong: the Majjhima Nikaya records the Buddha's debates with the Jains and Ajivikas.

st.3: The Murtipujakas are the idol-worshipping branch of the Svetambaras.

x: All three statements are correct: a Svetambara monk keeps 14 items while a Digambara keeps only a broom and water pot, the Svetambaras keep the 12 Angas while the Digambaras hold them lost, and the Murtipujakas are the idol-worshipping Svetambaras (the Sthanakvasis and Terapanthis reject idols).

st.3: The Vamsatthapakasini, which tells the Chanakya–Chandragupta legend, is a Buddhist commentary of the 10th century.

x: All three statements are correct: the Dipavamsa and Mahavamsa describe Ashoka's mission to Sri Lanka, the Vishnu Purana gives the Mauryan king lists, and the Vamsatthapakasini is a 10th-century Buddhist commentary on the Mahavamsa that tells the Chanakya–Chandragupta legend.

st.2: Skandagupta bore the titles Shakraditya and Mahendraditya.
st.3: Chandragupta II was a devotee of Kartikeya.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Shakraditya and Mahendraditya were titles of Kumaragupta I, not Skandagupta. Statement 3 is wrong: the devotee of Kartikeya was Kumaragupta I (peacock-type coins); Chandragupta II was a Vaishnava (Paramabhagavata). Statement 4 is wrong: Kumaragupta I's earliest record is the Bilsad inscription (415 CE).

st.2: Later dinaras contained more gold and less alloy.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: later Gupta dinaras contained less gold and more alloy. Statement 3 is wrong: silver coins were issued after the defeat of the Shakas (Western Kshatrapas) by Chandragupta II, not the Kushanas.

st.3: Aryabhata's Panchasiddhantika summarises five siddhantas, including the Paitamaha and Paulisa.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Brihat Jataka is a work on astrology (horoscopy), not medicine. Statement 3 is wrong: the Panchasiddhantika is Varahamihira's work, not Aryabhata's.

st.3: A candidate was not required to own a house of his own.
st.1: A candidate had to own at least one full veli of tax-paying land.
st.4: A person who had failed to submit accounts was disqualified, though his relatives remained eligible.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the minimum was one-fourth veli of tax-paying land. Statement 2 is wrong: the age limit was 35 to 70. Statement 3 is wrong: a candidate had to own a house on his own site. Statement 4 is wrong: a person who failed to submit accounts and his relatives were all disqualified.

st.1: Rajadhiraja I was made co-regent in 1012 and became king in 1014.
st.4: Rajaraja I as Ulakalanda Perumal was likened to Shiva measuring the earth in three strides.
st.2: Inscriptions praised the king as a warrior and patron of the arts but never as a protector of varnashrama dharma.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: it was Rajendra I who was made co-regent in 1012 and became king in 1014. Statement 2 is wrong: inscriptions also praised the king as protector of varnashrama dharma. Statement 3 is wrong: royal orders had a Sanskrit preamble and a Tamil operative part. Statement 4 is wrong: measuring the earth in three strides is Vishnu's (Trivikrama) feat, not Shiva's.

st.2: He rose to be the Malik Naib of Alauddin.

x: All three statements are correct: Malik Kafur was seized at Cambay by Nusrat Khan in 1299, rose to be Alauddin's Malik Naib, and was called Hazar Dinari because he had been bought for 1,000 dinars.

st.2: He allowed land revenue to be raised by up to one-half in a single year.
st.1: As Ghazi Malik he was Governor of Punjab under Balban.
st.3: Warangal fell to his forces in 1323 after a five-month siege and was renamed Daulatabad.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Ghazi Malik was Governor of Punjab (Dipalpur) under Alauddin Khalji, not Balban. Statement 2 is wrong: he limited any increase to about one-tenth (or one-eleventh). Statement 3 is wrong: Warangal was renamed Sultanpur; Daulatabad was the renamed Devagiri. Statement 4 is wrong: Prataparudra II died in the Narmada, not the Godavari.

st.2: His Gaz-i-Sikandari, a yard to measure land, was replaced by Sher Shah with the Ilahi gaz.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Gaz-i-Sikandari was used by Sher Shah and Akbar; the Ilahi gaz was introduced by Akbar. Statement 3 is wrong: the Sanskrit work he had translated into Persian was on medicine, not astronomy.

st.3: Under Firoz Tughlaq the efficiency of the army declined because iqtas became hereditary.

x: All three statements are correct: the iqta is the ancestor of the Mughal jagir and mansab system, its holder was the muqti or iqtadar, and under Firoz Tughlaq hereditary iqtas lowered the army's efficiency.

st.4: In Golconda Mustajir (tax-farming) rights were barred to Brahmins.
st.2: In Golconda the foreign Muslims were called Dakhnis.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the foreign Muslims were the Afaqis; the Dakhnis were the local Deccani Muslims. Statement 3 is wrong: the Bhadrachalam grants were made by Abul Hasan Qutb Shah (Tana Shah), not Ibrahim Qutb Shah. Statement 4 is wrong: Brahmins in Golconda did hold Mustajir rights.

st.3: He visited Andhra during the reign of Rudramadevi.

x: All three statements are correct: Marco Polo came from Venice, landed at Motupalli in 1292 and visited Andhra during the reign of the Kakatiya queen Rudramadevi.

st.1: Officers were transferred every few years so that they did not become entrenched.

x: All three statements are correct: Sher Shah's officers were transferred frequently to prevent entrenchment, 'dagh' was the branding of horses and 'chehra' the descriptive roll, and local headmen were made responsible for tracing crime.

st.2: A jagir gave its holder only the right to collect revenue, not ownership of the land.

x: All three statements are correct: khalisa was crown land feeding the imperial treasury, a jagir gave only the right to collect revenue and not ownership, and suyurghal was another name for charitable revenue-free grants.

st.3: Mahabat Khan seized Jahangir on the banks of the Jhelum in 1626.

x: All three statements are correct: Khusrau, son of Man Bai, rebelled in 1606 and was defeated near Lahore; Khurram revolted in 1622-26 after refusing to go to Kandahar; and Mahabat Khan seized Jahangir on the Jhelum in 1626.

st.2: Akbar had 15 subas in 1580 and 12 by the end of his reign.
st.1: The Chakla was prominent in Bengal under Sher Shah.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Chakla was prominent in Bengal under Murshid Quli Khan, not Sher Shah. Statement 2 is wrong: Akbar had 12 subas in 1580 and 15 by the end of his reign. Statement 3 is wrong: Aurangzeb's empire had 21 subas.

st.4: The tomb of Itimad-ud-Daula is the first tomb built wholly of red sandstone.
st.1: Sikandar Lodi's tomb, built by his son Ibrahim Lodi, has the first true arch.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Sikandar Lodi's tomb has the first double dome; the first true arch is in Balban's tomb. Statement 3 is wrong: the tomb of Itimad-ud-Daula was built by Nur Jahan for her father Mirza Ghiyas Beg. Statement 4 is wrong: it is the first tomb built wholly of white marble.

st.2: Balban's tomb had a double dome earlier.
st.1: Akbar's tomb at Sikandra has the first full Persian double dome in Mughal architecture.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the first full Persian double dome in Mughal architecture is in Humayun's tomb. Statement 2 is wrong: the earlier double dome is in Sikandar Lodi's tomb; Balban's tomb is known for the first true arch.

st.4: The Tirumurai, the Vaishnava canon called the 'Fifth Veda', consists of twelve books.
st.2: The Nayanars, devotees of Shiva, were traditionally sixty-three in number, all of them men.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the sixty-three Nayanars included three women, such as Karaikkal Ammaiyar. Statement 3 is wrong: the Nalayira Divya Prabandham was compiled by Nathamuni; Nambi Andar Nambi compiled the Tirumurai. Statement 4 is wrong: the Tirumurai is the Shaiva canon, not a Vaishnava one.

st.2: Chapter 12 of the Bhagavad Gita, the Bhakti Yoga, is part of the Shanti Parva of the Mahabharata.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Bhagavad Gita is part of the Bhishma Parva, not the Shanti Parva. Statement 3 is wrong: the Bhagavata Purana was composed in the Tamil south around the 9th-10th century, not in 12th-century Bengal.

st.3: Veerashaivism reached Andhra through Tikkana and Palkuriki Somanatha.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Telugu Basava Puranam was written by Palkuriki Somanatha. Statement 3 is wrong: Veerashaivism reached Andhra through Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya and Palkuriki Somanatha, not Tikkana.

st.3: Vallabhacharya's Pushtimarga, the 'path of grace', rejected householder life and demanded renunciation.
st.1: Nimbarka taught that God, souls and the world are eternally distinct.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: eternal distinction (Dvaita) is Madhvacharya's teaching; Nimbarka taught Dvaitadvaita. Statement 2 is wrong: Chaitanya's philosophy is Achintya Bhedabheda; Shuddhadvaita is Vallabha's. Statement 3 is wrong: the Pushtimarga accepted householder life.

st.4: Lahjat-i-Sikandar Shahi, a Persian rendering of Sanskrit music works, is linked with Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Chishtis were the chief patrons of sama, which the Naqshbandis opposed. Statement 4 is wrong: Lahjat-i-Sikandar Shahi is linked with Sikandar Lodi, not Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

st.3: Bahauddin Naqshband, founder of the Naqshbandi order, came to India and settled at Delhi.
st.1: The Qadiri order was founded by Abdul Qadir Jilani of Bukhara.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Abdul Qadir Jilani was of Baghdad. Statement 2 is wrong: the Qadiri order was brought to India by Shah Niamatullah and Makhdum Muhammad Jilani; Khwaja Baqi Billah introduced the Naqshbandi order. Statement 3 is wrong: Bahauddin Naqshband never came to India.

st.3: Masulipatnam
st.4: Mahe

x: The French founded Surat (1668), then Masulipatnam (1669), Pondicherry (1674), Mahe (1725) and Karaikal (1739): the order is 3, 2, 4, 1.

st.1: The Summary Revenue Settlement of 1856 was made with the taluqdars, setting aside the village proprietors.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 1856 settlement was made directly with the village proprietors, setting aside the taluqdars. Statement 3 is wrong: Wajid Ali Shah was exiled to Calcutta (Metiabruz), not Rangoon.

st.2: could employ other Europeans freely once he paid the subsidy.
st.1: was free to refuse a British Resident at his court.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the ruler had to accept a British Resident. Statement 2 is wrong: he could not employ other Europeans without the Company's consent. Statement 3 is wrong: he could not negotiate with other states without the Company's consent.

st.1: Under Mahalwari the unit of assessment was the individual ryot.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the unit of assessment was the mahal, a village or group of villages, not the individual ryot. Statement 2 is wrong: under Mahalwari the land belonged to the village community, not the government.

st.1: Lord Morley is called the 'Father of the Communal Electorate'.
st.4: The Congress first accepted them at Bombay in 1916.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Lord Minto, not Morley, is called the Father of the Communal Electorate. Statement 2 is wrong: the 1919 Act extended them to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans; the 1935 Act extended them to the depressed classes, women and labour. Statement 4 is wrong: the Congress accepted them at Lucknow in 1916.

st.4: It accepted the existing councils with nominated official majorities.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Lucknow Pact was a joint Congress–League scheme of reforms, not a merger of the two bodies. Statement 4 is wrong: the Pact demanded expanded councils with elected majorities.

st.3: P. Subbarayan became Premier in 1921.
st.1: The Congress contested the first elections under the 1919 Act and won a majority.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Congress boycotted the first elections under the 1919 Act. Statement 2 is wrong: the first Justice Party ministry (December 1920) was headed by A. Subbarayalu Reddiar. Statement 3 is wrong: it was the Raja of Panagal who became Premier in 1921.

st.1: The Government of India Act, 1935 provided for dyarchy at the Centre, which came into operation in 1937.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: dyarchy at the Centre under the 1935 Act never came into operation; only provincial autonomy began in 1937. Statement 3 is wrong: under the 1919 Act reserved subjects were run by the Governor and his executive council, not answerable to the legislature; transferred subjects were run by ministers.

st.1: Lord Wavell declared India a party to the war with Germany on 3 September 1939.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: it was Lord Linlithgow, not Wavell, who declared India a party to the war. Statement 4 is wrong: the Lahore Resolution was adopted on 23 March 1940.

st.2: The Government of India Act, 1935 is described as "constitutional autocracy".

x: All three statements are correct: irrigation and canals was a Provincial List entry, the 1935 Act is described as "constitutional autocracy", and India was governed by the 1935 Act, as adapted, until 26 January 1950.

st.2: His Widow Remarriage Association, usually dated 1861, was founded in Calcutta.
st.4: He held that social reform should wait until political freedom was won.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Widow Remarriage Association (1861) was founded in Bombay, not Calcutta. Statement 3 is wrong: the Deccan Education Society was founded by Tilak, Agarkar, Chiplunkar and others. Statement 4 is wrong: Ranade held that social and religious reform should proceed together with political progress; postponing social reform was Tilak's view.

st.2: Gurram Jashuva was known as 'Kavi Samrat'.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Jashuva was known as 'Kavi Kokila'; 'Kavi Samrat' is Viswanatha Satyanarayana. Statement 3 is wrong: Jashuva was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1970.

st.1: The Communal Award of 1932 gave the depressed classes a separate electorate with a double vote for 20 years.

x: All three statements are correct: the Communal Award gave the depressed classes a separate electorate with a double vote for 20 years, Gandhi began his fast at Yerwada on 20 September 1932, and the Poona Pact gave them 148 provincial seats and 18% of the Central Legislature.

st.3: National Youth Day is observed in India on his death anniversary.
st.2: He was born at Varanasi on 12 January 1863.
st.1: His birth name was Gadadhar Chattopadhyay.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: his birth name was Narendranath Datta; Gadadhar Chattopadhyay was Ramakrishna. Statement 2 is wrong: he was born at Calcutta. Statement 3 is wrong: National Youth Day (12 January) marks his birthday. Statement 4 is wrong: Sister Nivedita was Margaret Noble; Madeleine Slade was Gandhi's disciple Mirabehn.

st.3: It was directed mainly against Hindu landlords (jenmis) and the British.

x: All three statements are correct: the Moplah rising took place in Malabar in 1921, was led by Variyankunnathu Kunjahammad Haji and Ali Musliyar, and was directed mainly against the jenmi landlords and the British.

st.4: It caused the British less trouble in the region than the Non-Cooperation Movement.
st.3: It was a non-violent tribal satyagraha run by the Congress.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: its base was among the Koyas and Konda Doras of the Gudem hills, not the Bhils. Statement 3 is wrong: it was an armed tribal guerrilla war outside the Congress. Statement 4 is wrong: it gave the British more trouble in the region than the Non-Cooperation Movement.

st.3: Pattabhi Sitaramayya lost the 1939 Congress presidential election to Subhas Chandra Bose.

x: All three statements are correct: Pattabhi's 1935 history is the official history of the Congress, P. Ananda Charlu presided in 1891, and Pattabhi lost the 1939 presidential election to Subhas Chandra Bose.

st.1: He presided over the Karachi session (March 1931), where the resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme, drafted by Jawaharlal Nehru, was adopted.

x: All three statements are correct: Patel presided at Karachi (1931), where the Fundamental Rights resolution drafted by Nehru was adopted; he was President of the Gujarat PCC and headed the Parliamentary Board for 1937; and in the Interim Government he held Home with Information & Broadcasting.

st.1: The Dalai Lama fled to India in March 1962.
st.4: China's road through the Tawang tract was one of the causes of the 1962 war.
st.2: Goa was liberated through Operation Polo in December 1961.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Dalai Lama fled to India in March 1959. Statement 2 is wrong: Goa was liberated through Operation Vijay; Operation Polo was Hyderabad (1948). Statement 3 is wrong: China declared its unilateral ceasefire on 21 November 1962. Statement 4 is wrong: the road at issue ran through Aksai Chin, not Tawang.

st.2: Schedule C was left to the private sector.

x: All three statements are correct: Schedule A listed 17 industries reserved for the State, Schedule B 12 industries in which the State would increasingly set up units, and Schedule C was left to the private sector.

st.2: Around 1911 most District Judges in the Presidency were Telugus.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: around 1911 no District Judge was a Telugu (0 against 19). Statement 4 is wrong: Andhra's 8 colleges included no engineering, medical or law college.

st.1: The Andhra Jana Sangham (1921) grew into the Hyderabad State Congress.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Andhra Jana Sangham grew into the Nizam Andhra Mahasabha. Statement 3 is wrong: Swami Ramananda Tirtha launched the Join Indian Union movement on 7 August 1947.

st.2: At the first Andhra Mahasabha (1913) Nyapati Subbarao proposed one rule for all Telugu areas.
st.1: In 1912 Puchalapalli Sundarayya and Jonnavittula Gurunatham sketched a united Andhra.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 1912 sketch was by Unnava Lakshminarayana and Jonnavittula Gurunatham; Sundarayya came later. Statement 2 is wrong: Nyapati Subbarao's proposal came at the second Andhra Mahasabha (1914). Statement 3 is wrong: the Andhra Congress Swaraj Party manifesto was of 1936.

st.3: Kardamaka silver coins carried Vikrama-era dates.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: their principal coins were silver, not gold. Statement 3 is wrong: Kardamaka silver coins carried Saka-era dates.

st.3: The Gupta era of 319-320 AD is linked with Chandragupta I.

x: All three statements are correct: the Vikrama Samvat is also the Krit and Malav Samvat, the Saka era of 78 AD is linked with Kanishka and also Chashtana, and the Gupta era of 319-320 AD is linked with Chandragupta I.

st.2: He defeated Rudradaman and recovered Malwa, Saurashtra, Konkan and Nasik.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Gautamiputra Satakarni was a Satavahana; the Kshaharata was Nahapana. Statement 2 is wrong: he defeated Nahapana, not Rudradaman, who in fact defeated the Satavahanas later.

st.2: Women gave gifts at Bharhut, Sanchi and Amaravati only after naming their husbands or fathers.
st.4: Women were barred from titles such as Maharathini and Mahabhoji.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: women made independent gifts without naming husbands or fathers. Statement 3 is wrong: vetti by women is recorded in the Kamasutra, not the Arthashastra. Statement 4 is wrong: women did bear titles such as Maharathini and Mahabhoji.

st.2: It had a special vihara for monks from Sri Lanka.

x: All three statements are correct: as Vijayapuri it was the Ikshvaku capital with Hariti as tutelary goddess, it had a special vihara for Sri Lankan monks, and the first structural Hindu temples of Andhra were built there.

st.3: The Kurkyala inscription of his son Jinavallabha contains early Telugu verses.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Pampa's Adipurana describes the life of Rishabhadeva, the first tirthankara, not Mahavira. Statement 3 is wrong: Jinavallabha, author of the Kurkyala inscription, was Pampa's brother, not his son.

st.3: The Kailasa temple at Ellora is built in the Dravida style.

x: All three statements are correct: the Kailasa temple of Krishna I is Cave 16 at Ellora, Govinda III's Himalayan campaign is in the Sanjan plates, and the Kailasa is in the Dravida style.

st.1: Manumasiddhi II was the first king at Nellore, as the Taruvariyur inscription shows.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Taruvariyur inscription shows Manumasiddhi I as the first king at Nellore. Statement 3 is wrong: Samantabhoja won at Palaiyuru; Muttukur (1263) is where Manumasiddhi II was killed.

st.2: His title Mlecchabdhi Kumbodbhava is recorded in the Kurkyala inscription.
st.3: He took the title Nissivu Bhudana Parasurama for his land gifts to Buddhist viharas.
st.1: He took the title Andhra Bhoja.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Andhra Bhoja was Krishnadevaraya's title; Prolaya Vema took Dharma Durgavibhala. Statement 2 is wrong: Mlecchabdhi Kumbodbhava is recorded in the Mallavaram inscription. Statement 3 is wrong: Nissivu Bhudana Parasurama was for his land gifts to Brahmanas. Statement 4 is wrong: the Mutnuri inscription dates the Patala Ganga steps to 1346.

st.3: Kshetrayya, composer of the Movva padams, flourished in his reign.

x: All three statements are correct: Abdullah came to the throne in 1626 and had the longest reign with Hayat Bakshi Begum, accepted Mughal suzerainty by the Inqiyad Nama (1636), and Kshetrayya flourished in his reign.

st.1: The Talari policed the towns.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Talari policed the village. Statement 2 is wrong: the Kavali Daru policed the sthala; the towns were under the Peta Kavalidaru.

st.1: The Praja Socialist Party was formed in September 1952 by merging the KMPP with the Communist Party.
st.3: In 1953 Tirupati was chosen as the capital of Andhra State, though the PSP wanted Kurnool.
st.2: Tenneti Viswanatham left the Congress in 1951 and joined the Swatantra Party.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the PSP merged the KMPP with the Socialist Party. Statement 2 is wrong: Tenneti joined the Kisan Mazdoor Party; the Swatantra Party came only in 1959. Statement 3 is wrong: Kurnool was chosen, though the PSP wanted Tirupati. Statement 4 is wrong: the Krishikar Lok Party won 22 seats.

st.3: The Brahmaiah Award covered 142 villages.

x: All three statements are correct: Munagala was then in Nandigama taluk of Krishna district, the agitation was withdrawn on 19 June 1939, and the Brahmaiah Award covered 142 villages.

st.2: The Sribagh Pact (1937) gave Telangana and Nellore irrigation priority for 10 years or as long as needed.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Sribagh Pact gave the priority to Rayalaseema and Nellore, not Telangana. Statement 3 is wrong: the Tungabhadra Board was constituted under Section 66(4) of the Andhra State Act, 1953.

st.3: It presents the poet as a loyal court flatterer content with royal patronage.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Firdausi was written by Gurram Jashuva, not Sri Sri. Statement 3 is wrong: it presents the poet as a rebel against patronage.

st.2: His minister Kautilya split the Lichchhavi chiefs.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Lichchhavi chiefs were split by Ajatashatru's minister Vassakara; Kautilya was Chandragupta Maurya's minister. Statement 3 is wrong: the mahashilakantaka was a catapult hurling stones; the chariot fitted with a mace was the rathamusala.

st.3: The Kushana gold dinara followed the Roman weight standard of about 16 g (240 grains).
st.2: Vima Kadphises' gold coins show Vishnu with a trident and a bull.
st.1: Kujula Kadphises issued gold coins imitating Roman coins.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Kujula Kadphises issued copper coins; Vima Kadphises first issued gold. Statement 2 is wrong: the figure with the trident and bull is Shiva. Statement 3 is wrong: the dinara weighed about 8 g (120 grains). Statement 4 is wrong: Kanishka's legends are in the Greek script (Bactrian language), not Brahmi.

st.2: The guilds carried on long-distance and overseas trade.

x: All three statements are correct: the guilds grew more independent as Chola power declined, carried on long-distance and overseas trade, and had their own code, symbols and militias and acted as bankers.

st.2: He entered Nadiya in 1204 and drove Ballala Sena to East Bengal.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the king driven out of Nadiya was Lakshmana Sena, not Ballala Sena. Statement 3 is wrong: his Tibet expedition was a disaster.

st.4: The Assam Prohibition of Polygamy Bill, 2025 makes polygamy cognizable and non-bailable, with up to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: under the 1939 Act the ground is non-payment of maintenance for 2 years. Statement 4 is wrong: the Assam Bill provides up to 7 years' rigorous imprisonment.

st.3: The Scheduled Castes Order covered Sikhs from 1956, and Buddhists were added in 1990.

x: All three statements are correct: the Arzal are the lowest group among Indian Muslims, Indian Christians trace their faith to St Thomas (52 AD), and the SC Order was extended to Sikhs in 1956 and Buddhists in 1990.

st.1: The four hereditary varnas crystallised in the Later Vedic period.

x: All three statements are correct: the hereditary varnas crystallised in the Later Vedic period, the post-Maurya and Gupta age saw the Manu Smriti and rigid caste, and Dumont's Homo Hierarchicus appeared in 1966.

st.2: Taking part in the wider society while retaining identity
st.1: Spread of culture, e.g. through media

x: Integration is taking part in the wider society while retaining identity, cultural relativism is understanding a culture on its own terms, xenocentrism is preferring other cultures, and cultural diffusion is the spread of culture: A-2, B-3, C-4, D-1.

st.4: Visakhapatnam had the largest rural population.
st.1: Its urban share fell from 29.47% in 2001 to 24.13% in 2011.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the urban share rose from 24.13% (2001) to 29.47% (2011). Statement 2 is wrong: Visakhapatnam (47.45%) was the most urbanised, ahead of Krishna. Statement 4 is wrong: East Godavari had the largest rural population.

st.4: PM-DAKSH is a housing scheme for Scheduled Castes.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the ₹2.5 lakh is not paid at once – ₹1.5 lakh goes to the joint account and ₹1 lakh as a fixed deposit. Statement 4 is wrong: PM-DAKSH is a skilling scheme, not a housing scheme.

st.4: The 1984 riots in Hyderabad's old city followed the Rameeza Bee case.
st.2: It was completed in 1693 by Abul Hasan Tana Shah.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Mecca Masjid was completed in 1693 by Aurangzeb; Tana Shah had lost Golconda in 1687. Statement 4 is wrong: the riots after the Rameeza Bee case were in 1978.

st.3: It provides for a special court only in the State capital.
st.1: It was a response to the 2012 Delhi gang rape (Nirbhaya case).

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Disha Bill responded to the 2019 Hyderabad veterinarian rape-murder. Statement 2 is wrong: the 21 days are 7 days of investigation and 14 days of trial. Statement 3 is wrong: it provides for a special court in every district.

st.3: It allows 2 months for investigation of rape.

x: All three statements are correct: the 2018 Act raised the minimum punishment for rape from 7 to 10 years, bars anticipatory bail for rape of a girl below 16, and sets 2 months for investigation.

st.4: The legal age of marriage is 18 for both women and men.
st.3: The Madhya Pradesh High Court asked the Centre to lower the age of consent to 14, citing early puberty due to social-media exposure.

x: Statement 1 is correct: the Justice Verma Committee wanted the age of consent at 16. Statement 2 is wrong: the Law Commission's 283rd Report (2023) advised against lowering the age of consent under POCSO. Statement 3 is wrong: the Madhya Pradesh High Court asked for 16, not 14. Statement 4 is wrong: the marriage age is 18 for women and 21 for men.

st.2: The share of Bills referred to parliamentary committees fell from 71% in the 15th Lok Sabha to 16% in the 17th.

x: All three statements are correct: Question Hour is the most effective control over the executive, committee referrals fell from 71% (15th Lok Sabha) to 16% (17th), and delays by Governors and Speakers are an accountability gap.

st.1: The Code on Wages, 2019 is the first law to recognise aggregators, gig and platform workers.
st.4: NITI estimated 7.7 crore gig workers in 2020-21.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the first law to recognise them is the Code on Social Security, 2020. Statement 2 is wrong: registration gives no employee status. Statement 4 is wrong: NITI estimated 77 lakh gig workers in 2020-21.

st.1: The Indira Awaas Yojana began in 1985 and became an independent scheme only in 2016.
st.3: PMAY-Gramin converges with MGNREGS (60/75 person-days of unskilled work) and the SBM-G toilet.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: IAY became independent in 1996 and was restructured into PMAY-G in 2016. Statement 2 is wrong: PMAY-G is run by the Ministry of Rural Development. Statement 3 is wrong: the MGNREGS convergence is 90/95 person-days.

st.1: It was launched in August 2020.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: ABDM was launched in September 2021; August 2020 was only the NDHM pilot. Statement 2 is wrong: the Healthcare Professionals Registry covers both modern and traditional medicine.

st.1: It was adopted in 1919.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Convention No. 102 (social security minimum standards) was adopted in 1952. Statement 2 is wrong: India has not ratified it.

st.3: The 16th Finance Commission found AP lowest among States in per-capita social pension spending.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 16th Finance Commission found AP highest in per-capita social pension spending. Statement 4 is wrong: the Mukhyamantri Vriddhajan Pension Yojana is Bihar's scheme.

st.4: It described the Ashraf as the most deprived group of Muslims.
st.1: It was set up in March 2005 and submitted its report in November 2007.
st.2: It found Muslims adequately represented in public employment but behind in higher education.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the report came in November 2006. Statement 2 is wrong: it found Muslims under-represented in public employment as well. Statement 3 is wrong: it proposed an Equal Opportunity Commission, not a linguistic minorities body. Statement 4 is wrong: it named the Arzal, not the Ashraf, as the most deprived.

st.3: It came into force on 19 April 2017.

x: All three statements are correct: the 2016 Act replaced the welfare-based 1995 Act, Section 2(s) defines a person with disability by long-term impairment, and it came into force on 19 April 2017.

st.1: Before 2019, J&K had no separate Constitution, and all Union laws applied to it automatically.
st.4: Article 370 lies in Part XVIII of the Constitution, which deals with emergency provisions.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: J&K had its own Constitution and only defence, external affairs and communications applied automatically. Statement 3 is wrong: Gilgit-Baltistan is a political status and sovereignty issue, not a border-demarcation dispute. Statement 4 is wrong: Article 370 is in Part XXI (temporary provisions).

st.3: Red Flag is a US Navy multinational exercise.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Yudh Abhyas is an army exercise. Statement 3 is wrong: Red Flag is a US Air Force exercise, not a Navy one.

st.1: It was revived under the Nalanda University Act, 2014.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: it was revived under the Nalanda University Act, 2010. Statement 2 is wrong: the new campus inaugurated in June 2024 is at Rajgir, not Bodh Gaya.

st.2: India took command of Combined Task Force 154, headquartered in Bahrain, for the first time in 2026.

x: All three statements are correct: IFC-IOR was set up in December 2018 at Gurugram with IMAC, India first commanded CTF-154 (HQ Bahrain) in 2026, and the Djibouti Code of 2009 is an anti-piracy code India observes since 2020.

st.1: Like the British Parliament, the Indian Parliament is sovereign; its law-making power is not limited by a written Constitution.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: unlike Britain's, the Indian Parliament is not sovereign and is limited by a written Constitution. Statement 3 is wrong: Britain has a hereditary monarch, not an elected head of State.

st.1: It combined the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's Council for the first time.
st.3: It threw the civil services open to competition, worked out by the Aitchison Committee (1886).

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 1853 Act separated the legislative and executive functions. Statement 2 is wrong: it added six legislative members. Statement 3 is wrong: the open competition was worked out by the Macaulay Committee (1854).

st.3: Article 51A(a) names the National Flag and the National Anthem, but not the National Song.

x: All three statements are correct: the full Anthem takes about 52 seconds, Vande Mataram was declared the National Song on 24 January 1950, and Article 51A(a) names the Flag and the Anthem but not the National Song.

st.2: First Amendment creating the Ninth Schedule
st.1: Waman Rao case

x: The First Amendment (1951) created the Ninth Schedule, Kesavananda Bharati came in 1973, Waman Rao in 1981 and I.R. Coelho in 2007: the order is 2, 4, 1, 3.

st.1: Charged expenditure can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India without an Appropriation Act.
st.3: Amendments may vary the amount or alter the destination of a voted grant.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: every withdrawal, even for charged expenditure, needs an Appropriation Act. Statement 2 is wrong: it is a Money Bill that the Rajya Sabha cannot amend. Statement 3 is wrong: no amendment may vary the amount or alter the destination of a grant.

st.1: The President cannot pardon a death sentence; he can only commute it.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the President can pardon a death sentence (Article 72). Statement 2 is wrong: only the President, not the Governor, can pardon a court-martial sentence.

st.2: Its Act lapsed on 29 February 2004, after which the Commission was wound up.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: after the 1993 Act lapsed in 2004 the Commission was not wound up; it continues as a non-statutory body. Statement 3 is wrong: it is a non-statutory body, not a constitutional one.

st.4: It is reconstituted every five years.
st.2: It can take up research only on references from the Central Government.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it also takes up research suo motu. Statement 3 is wrong: its report goes to the Ministry of Law and Justice. Statement 4 is wrong: it is reconstituted every three years.

st.1: CEDAW was adopted in 1989 and ratified by India in 1993.
st.3: India has signed but not acceded to the CRC.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: CEDAW was adopted in 1979. Statement 2 is wrong: India signed the Convention against Torture in 1997 but has not ratified it. Statement 3 is wrong: India acceded to the CRC on 11 December 1992.

st.4: More than 1,000 RTI activists had been killed by July 2026.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Economic Survey suggested exempting draft policy discussions, not disclosing them. Statement 4 is wrong: the figure is more than 100, not 1,000.

st.3: Such a request must be made within 7 days of the results.

x: All three statements are correct: the Court rejected 100% VVPAT counting, second- and third-placed candidates may seek checks of 5% of EVMs, and the request must be made within 7 days of the results.

st.3: Among the States short of 50 per cent, Haryana has the lowest share at 42.12 per cent.

x: All three statements are correct: Bihar was first with 50% (2006), about 49.75% of the 24.41 lakh PRI representatives are women, and Haryana has the lowest share (42.12%).

st.2: Drone mapping under SVAMITVA is done by ISRO and NICSI.
st.1: The SVAMITVA scheme was launched on 2 October 2020.
st.4: Andhra Pradesh scored 72.23 in the Devolution Index 2024.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: SVAMITVA was launched on 24 April 2020. Statement 2 is wrong: drone mapping is by the Survey of India and NICSI. Statement 3 is wrong: Karnataka ranked first. Statement 4 is wrong: AP scored 54.43; 72.23 was Karnataka's score.

st.3: In 2025 India ranked 131st of 148, and Iceland topped the index.

x: All three statements are correct: India was 108th of 149 in 2018, 127th of 146 in 2023, and 131st of 148 in 2025, when Iceland topped the index.

st.1: Local Government is a subject in the State List.

x: All three statements are correct: Local Government is in the State List, Article 243ZF let inconsistent municipal laws continue for at most one year, and Part IXB was added by the 97th Amendment, 2011.

st.3: The DICGC, a wholly-owned RBI subsidiary set up in 1978, insures bank deposits but not deposits with NBFCs.

x: All three statements are correct: NBFCs and NaBFID are RBI-regulated, the NHB was set up in 1988 under the 1987 Act, and the DICGC insures bank deposits, not NBFC deposits.

st.3: At NAeG 2026, Rohini Gram Panchayat (Dhule, Maharashtra) won the Silver.
st.1: The 2015 awards had the first-ever dedicated category for Gram Panchayats.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the first dedicated Gram Panchayat category came in the 2025 awards. Statement 3 is wrong: Rohini Gram Panchayat won the Gold; e-Jagriti won the Silver. Statement 4 is wrong: the awards began in 2003.

st.1: Narendra Modi's visit to Israel in July 2017 marked 30 years of full diplomatic ties.
st.4: The 1988 action plan for nuclear disarmament is associated with Indira Gandhi.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: full ties date from 1992, so 2017 marked 25 years. Statement 2 is wrong: full relations were established in 1992 under P.V. Narasimha Rao. Statement 4 is wrong: the 1988 action plan is Rajiv Gandhi's.

st.4: The Pakistan army surrendered in Chittagong on 16 December 1971.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Katchatheevu was ceded in 1974. Statement 4 is wrong: the surrender took place in Dhaka.

st.2: The Act received Presidential assent on 2 February 2006.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Act received assent on 5 September 2005; 2 February 2006 was its launch. Statement 4 is wrong: it began in 200 districts and covered all 625 districts only from 1 April 2008.

st.4: Deepam-2 gives 2 free LPG cylinders a year.
st.2: Annadata Sukhibhava gives farmers ₹6,000 a year.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Annadata Sukhibhava gives ₹20,000 a year. Statement 3 is wrong: Aadabidda Nidhi gives ₹1,500 a month. Statement 4 is wrong: Deepam-2 gives 3 free cylinders.

st.2: Under the new series, India's GDP at constant (2022-23) prices in 2024-25 was Rs 318.07 lakh crore.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Rs 318.07 lakh crore is GDP at current prices, not constant prices. Statement 3 is wrong: in the 2025-26 estimates nominal growth (8.0%) exceeded real growth (7.4%), not the other way round.

st.3: In May 2026, MoSPI issued a uniform guideline for compiling GSVA with 2022-23 as the base year.

x: All three statements are correct: APSES 2024-25 figures are at 2011-12 prices, manufacturing GVA was allocated to States by ASI shares, and MoSPI's May 2026 guideline uses 2022-23 as the GSVA base year.

st.2: Nationalisation of 14 banks
st.3: Setting up of SIDBI

x: Fourteen banks were nationalised in 1969, the first RRB (Prathama Grameen Bank) came in 1975, NABARD in 1982 and SIDBI in 1990: the order is 2, 1, 4, 3.

st.3: Bina Agarwal shared the Leontief Prize with Daniel Kahneman for work on gender, land rights and environment.

x: All three statements are correct: Mahbub ul Haq built the HDI on Sen's capability ideas, Sen wrote both books, and Bina Agarwal shared the Leontief Prize with Daniel Kahneman.

st.1: The Dandekar and Rath study (1971) used NSS data of 1970-71.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Dandekar and Rath used NSS data of 1960-61. Statement 3 is wrong: the Alagh Task Force reported in 1979, not 1989.

st.1: Plans I to XI averaged about 1% growth, against about 4.5% before Independence.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Plans averaged about 4.5% growth against about 1% before Independence. Statement 3 is wrong: regional disparities persist and are counted a failure of planning.

st.2: The expression 'Licence-Permit-Quota Raj' was coined by C. Rajagopalachari.

x: All three statements are correct: Narasimha Rao (PM from 21 June 1991) is called the father of the reforms, Rajagopalachari coined 'Licence-Permit-Quota Raj', and Manmohan Singh was Finance Minister in 1991.

st.2: Brownfield assets are leased to private parties, with ownership staying with the government.

x: All three statements are correct: the NMP was launched in August 2021 with ₹6 lakh crore over FY2022-25, brownfield assets are leased with ownership retained, and roads (27%), railways (25%) and power (15%) lead.

st.2: Article 275 grants are not meant for financing every Centrally Sponsored Scheme.

x: All three statements are correct: tax devolution is under Article 270, Article 275 grants cover revenue deficits, local bodies and disasters rather than every CSS, and Article 123 (ordinances) is not a transfer channel.

st.2: Under the 16th FC, the share of grants in FC transfers rose from 8.3% to 19.4%.
st.1: The 15th FC's revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants totalled about ₹9.47 lakh crore.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 15th FC grants totalled about ₹10.1 lakh crore; ₹9.47 lakh crore is the 16th FC total. Statement 2 is wrong: the share fell from 19.4% to 8.3%. Statement 3 is wrong: the 16th FC discontinued sector-specific grants.

st.4: A score of 90 or more earns a State the 'Achiever' category.
st.1: All 17 goals were scored quantitatively.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: 16 goals were scored and SDG 17 was assessed only qualitatively. Statement 3 is wrong: Front Runner needs 65-99; 60 is a Performer. Statement 4 is wrong: only a score of 100 earns 'Achiever'.

st.3: The ₹2,000 notes withdrawn in May 2023 continue to be legal tender.

x: All three statements are correct: curbing counterfeit currency was an objective, the Supreme Court upheld the move 4:1 in 2023, and the withdrawn ₹2,000 notes remain legal tender.

st.1: According to NCRB's Crime in India 2024, fake Indian currency worth about ₹54.61 crore was seized.

x: All three statements are correct: NCRB reports about ₹54.61 crore of fake currency seized, about 99.3% of the specified notes came back, and the 2017 Act ended the liability on the old notes.

st.1: They acquire NPAs, generally at a premium.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: ARCs buy NPAs at a discount, not a premium. Statement 2 is wrong: ARCs are regulated by the RBI, not SEBI.

st.3: Global Systemically Important Banks are identified by the IMF, and no Indian bank is among them.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the D-SIBs are SBI, ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank; Axis Bank is not one. Statement 3 is wrong: G-SIBs are identified by the Financial Stability Board, not the IMF.

st.2: The net NPA ratio was 2.5% in September 2025.
st.4: DICGC insures deposits up to ₹1 lakh per depositor per bank.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the net NPA ratio was 0.5%. Statement 3 is wrong: the CRAR was 17.3% in March 2025. Statement 4 is wrong: the DICGC cover is ₹5 lakh; ₹1 lakh was the old limit.

st.2: Bharat Dal, launched with chana dal in July 2023, was later extended to moong dal.

x: All three statements are correct: the PSF (March 2015) began with onion and potato, Bharat Dal was extended from chana to moong dal, and under OMSS the FCI sells wheat and rice.

st.1: Interest takes 40 paise of every rupee spent in Union Budget 2026-27.
st.2: States had borrowed ₹5.23 trillion by October 2025, about 92% of their FY26 plan.
st.4: Andhra Pradesh's fiscal deficit in 2024-25 was 3.05% of GSDP, within the 4% limit.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: interest takes 20 paise of every rupee spent (it is about 40% of revenue receipts). Statement 2 is wrong: the borrowing was about 62% of the plan. Statement 3 is wrong: the RBI wants a shift from subsidies to capital expenditure. Statement 4 is wrong: AP's deficit was 5.05% of GSDP, above the 4% limit.

st.2: Under GST 2.0, the 28% rate applies to sin and ultra-luxury goods.
st.4: Rates can be changed only by an amendment of the GST Acts passed by Parliament.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: under GST 2.0 sin and ultra-luxury goods attract 40%; the 28% slab was removed. Statement 3 is wrong: the statutory CGST ceiling is 20% (40% for IGST). Statement 4 is wrong: rates are changed by notification on the Council's recommendation within the ceilings.

st.2: The Centre's vote carries two-thirds of the weight in the GST Council.
st.1: Petroleum and electricity have been brought under GST.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: petroleum and electricity remain outside GST. Statement 2 is wrong: the Centre has one-third of the weight, which is enough to block a three-fourths decision. Statement 3 is wrong: Mohit Minerals held the Council's recommendations persuasive, not binding.

st.1: The capital account includes the Balance of Trade.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Balance of Trade is part of the current account. Statement 2 is wrong: FDI is recorded in the capital account.

st.3: It was constituted in 2004 under M.S. Swaminathan.

x: All three statements are correct: its C2 cost adds imputed family labour, rent and interest to A2, it recommended a National Agricultural Risk Fund, and it was constituted in 2004.

st.3: They draw refinance from NABARD.

x: All three statements are correct: RRBs are sponsored by Scheduled Commercial Banks, are overseen by NABARD and draw refinance from NABARD.

st.2: Assistance of up to Rs 30 lakh is given per mandi.
st.1: It is a Centrally Sponsored scheme funded through NABARD's RIDF.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: e-NAM is a Central Sector scheme funded through the Agri-Tech Infrastructure Fund. Statement 2 is wrong: assistance is up to Rs 75 lakh per mandi. Statement 3 is wrong: payment goes online directly to the farmer, not through a commission agent.

st.3: Antyodaya Anna Yojana provides 35 kg of foodgrain per family per month to the poorest.

x: All three statements are correct: rationing began in the 1940s with the Bengal famine, the RPDS was launched in June 1992, and AAY gives 35 kg per family per month.

st.1: Lignite is counted in place of raw coal.
st.2: Only pig iron output is used for steel.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the coal component counts coal production, not lignite. Statement 2 is wrong: the steel component uses steel output, not pig iron alone.

st.2: Each strategic sector keeps 1 to 4 CPSEs.

x: All three statements are correct: the 2021 policy has 4 strategic sectors, each keeps 1 to 4 CPSEs, and the Economic Survey 2025-26 says the stake in listed CPSEs may fall to 26%.

st.3: In August 2022 the Union Power Ministry, under Section 92 of APRA, ordered APGENCO to pay about ₹6,756 crore to Telangana.
st.2: The CAG found power-subsidy spending at 81% of budget estimates in 2023.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the CAG found spending at 121% of the estimates. Statement 3 is wrong: the order was for Telangana to pay APGENCO, not the reverse. Statement 4 is wrong: the Telangana High Court quashed the order in October 2023.

st.3: Interest payments are non-developmental expenditure.

x: All three statements are correct: interest was about Rs 14,783 crore in 2017-18 (RE), it has more than doubled since, and it is non-developmental expenditure.

st.3: In 2024-25, total central resources stayed below BE despite EAP loans, as grants fell short.
st.4: APSES 2024-25 says the flow of funds from GoI was higher than anticipated.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: AP relies more on grants than the average State. Statement 3 is wrong: total central resources rose above BE because of EAP loans, though grants fell short. Statement 4 is wrong: APSES cites a lesser than anticipated flow of funds from GoI as a fiscal stress.

st.3: It covers 13.49 lakh farmers.

x: All three statements are correct: APMIP has run since 2003-04, Rayalaseema has 71 per cent of its coverage, and it covers 13.49 lakh farmers (37.90 lakh acres).

st.1: It provides Rs 13,500 per farmer family per year.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: it gives Rs 20,000 a year; Rs 13,500 was the old YSR Rythu Bharosa amount. Statement 3 is wrong: the Rabi instalment is Rs 7,000.

st.1: It earmarks 10% of land in new industrial parks for MSMEs.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the policy earmarks 33% of land in new parks for MSMEs. Statement 2 is wrong: it targets a minimum 30% industry share of GSDP.

st.2: The SEZ Act received the President's assent on 10 February 2006.
st.4: The SEZ Act and the SEZ Rules came into force on 23 June 2005.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: assent came on 23 June 2005. Statement 3 is wrong: the 2025 cut was to 10 hectares. Statement 4 is wrong: the Act and Rules came into force on 10 February 2006.

st.3: In its first year, MeeSeva training was given through radio broadcasts on All India Radio.
st.1: eSeva (2001), India's first integrated citizen service centres, was launched under Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: eSeva was launched under N. Chandrababu Naidu. Statement 2 is wrong: MeeSeva grew out of eSeva, not APSWAN. Statement 3 is wrong: first-year training was through television with MANA TV.

st.1: The resurvey under Jagananna Saswatha Bhu Hakku and Bhu Raksha began in December 2016.
st.2: The resurvey has covered all of the State's villages using drones, CORS and GIS.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the resurvey began in December 2020. Statement 2 is wrong: it has covered 6,901 villages, not all. Statement 3 is wrong: the new passbooks carry the State emblem, not the Chief Minister's photograph.

st.3: It is implemented by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.

x: All three statements are correct: SVAMITVA gives Property Cards to village households, uses drone surveys, and is run by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.

st.1: The Club of Rome, which first advocated resource conservation systematically at the international level, was founded in 1968 in Stockholm.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Club of Rome was founded in Rome. Statement 3 is wrong: the WCED was chaired by Gro Harlem Brundtland, Prime Minister of Norway, not Sweden.

st.2: BSE was India's first fully automated electronic exchange.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: NSE, not BSE, was the first fully automated electronic exchange. Statement 3 is wrong: India INX at GIFT City is regulated by IFSCA, not SEBI.

st.1: A finfluencer giving stock tips or return claims need not register with SEBI.
st.4: AP MSME Development Corporation and NSE ran an SME IPO awareness programme in Visakhapatnam.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: such finfluencers must register with SEBI. Statement 2 is wrong: the tick mark was introduced with Google, not Apple. Statement 4 is wrong: the programme was held in Vijayawada.

st.3: A parsec is larger than a light year.

x: All three statements are correct: a light year is about 9.46 trillion km, sunlight takes about 8 minutes 19 seconds to reach the Earth, and a parsec (about 3.26 light years) is larger than a light year.

st.1: A planet may orbit another planet instead of the Sun.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: under the IAU definition a planet must orbit the Sun; a body orbiting a planet is a satellite. Statement 3 is wrong: having a natural satellite is not a condition (the third is clearing its orbit).

st.2: Venus and Uranus are the only planets that rotate in the opposite direction.

x: All three statements are correct: the Earth rotates west to east (counter-clockwise seen from above the North Pole), Venus and Uranus have retrograde rotation, and the axis is tilted 23½° from the perpendicular.

st.1: GMT is the mean solar time at Paris.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: GMT is the mean solar time at Greenwich, not Paris. Statement 2 is wrong: UTC is based on atomic clocks, adjusted by leap seconds, not on solar observation alone.

st.2: Alfred Wegener proposed mantle convection currents in the 1930s, with heat from radioactive decay.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: mantle convection was proposed by Arthur Holmes, not Wegener. Statement 4 is wrong: Vine and Matthews (1963) gave magnetic-stripe evidence for sea-floor spreading; continental drift was Wegener's theory.

st.1: The zone factor of Zone II is 0.36 and that of Zone V is 0.10.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Zone V has the factor 0.36 and Zone II 0.10, not the reverse. Statement 2 is wrong: Zone III has a factor of 0.16; 0.24 is Zone IV.

st.3: Oxbow lakes are typical features of the lower course.

x: All three statements are correct: the upper course has vertical erosion and V-shaped valleys, the middle course lateral erosion and transport, and oxbow lakes form in the lower course.

st.2: Isobars are lines joining places having equal atmospheric pressure.

x: All three statements are correct: standard sea-level pressure is 1013.25 mb, isobars join places of equal pressure, and closely spaced isobars mean a steep gradient and strong winds.

st.3: Temperate cyclones cover a smaller area with stronger winds.

st.3: The Wayanad (Kerala) disaster of 2024 was a landslide.

st.4: Nellore in Karnataka is a major mica belt.

x: All three statements are correct: A&N recorded the lowest TFR (0.9), Bihar the highest (2.7), and 31 of the 36 States/UTs were below 2.1.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: most SCs work as marginal farmers and landless labourers. Statement 2 is wrong: SC unemployment (5.5%) was higher than the national rate (5%).

st.1: ISRO has launched 433 foreign satellites of more than 64 countries.

st.1: It was proclaimed by ECOSOC in 2007 by Resolution 62/136.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Resolution 62/136 (2007) was adopted by the UN General Assembly, not ECOSOC. Statement 3 is wrong: UN Women is headquartered in New York.

st.2: Aero India was first held in 1996 and is held every year.
st.3: iDEX was set up in 2021.
st.1: Aero India 2027, the 16th edition, will be held at AFS Hindan, Ghaziabad.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Aero India 2027 is at AFS Yelahanka, Bengaluru. Statement 2 is wrong: it is biennial. Statement 3 is wrong: iDEX was set up in 2018. Statement 4 is wrong: the defence corridors are in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

st.3: International Translation Day is observed on 30 September.

x: All three statements are correct: World Rivers Day is the fourth Sunday of September, Disarmament Week begins on UN Day (24 October), and International Translation Day is 30 September.

st.2: The National Green Tribunal was established on 2 June 2010.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the NGT was established on 18 October 2010; 2 June 2010 is when the Act was passed. Statement 3 is wrong: NITI Aayog came into existence on 1 January 2015.

st.2: India marks the day as Swachh Vayu Diwas, when the Swachh Survekshan awards are given.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the day was set in 2019 but first observed in 2020. Statement 2 is wrong: the awards given that day are the Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan awards, not Swachh Survekshan.

st.1: World Humanitarian Day (19 August) marks the 2003 bombing of the UN headquarters in Kabul.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the day marks the 2003 bombing of the UN headquarters in Baghdad. Statement 3 is wrong: National Handloom Day marks the Swadeshi Movement of 1905.

st.2: Dr. Rajendra Prasad Khajuria, a 1991 IFS officer of the AP cadre, became Director of the Wildlife Institute of India, Dehradun.
st.3: The Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy moved to Hyderabad in 1985.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the SPG was set up in 1985 but functions under the SPG Act, 1988. Statement 2 is wrong: Khajuria became Director of IGNFA, Dehradun. Statement 3 is wrong: the SVPNPA moved to Hyderabad in 1975.

st.1: Jagdish Kumar Mamidala became Chairman of the Board of Governors of IIM Calcutta, established in 1961.

x: All three statements are correct: Mamidala became Chairman of IIM Calcutta (est. 1961), Raghuvanshi was re-appointed DCGI for one year, and the GRMB was set up under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.

st.2: The title 'Vishva Vaidya Divyang Bandhu' was conferred on him by the Prime Minister of Mauritius.

x: All three statements are correct: Dr Guduru Jagadish formerly headed TTD's BIRRD Trust Hospital, the title was given by Mauritius PM Ramgoolam, and he was honoured for free polio camps.

st.3: Her term as IOC President is of eight years, up to 2033.

x: All three statements are correct: Kirsty Coventry took office as the 10th IOC President on 23 June 2025 in Lausanne, received the key from Thomas Bach, and has an eight-year term to 2033.

st.2: The Centre gives a grant of up to Rs 1,000 crore per park.

x: All three statements are correct: BHAVYA Rasayan plans three chemical parks, the Centre gives up to Rs 1,000 crore per park, and each covers at least 8 sq km (2,000 acres).

st.3: GDP is obtained as GVA plus taxes on products minus subsidies on products.

x: All three statements are correct: GDP grew 7.7% in 2025–26 against 7.1%, GVA grew 7.9%, and GDP equals GVA plus product taxes minus product subsidies.

st.3: Walnuts, almonds and Chilgoza pine nuts are the focus crops for the North-East region.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: agarwood is promoted in the North-East, not the Himalayan region. Statement 3 is wrong: walnuts, almonds and Chilgoza are the Himalayan region's crops.

st.3: The first Budget of the Republic was presented by John Matthai.

x: All three statements are correct: R.K. Shanmukham Chetty presented the first Budget on 26 November 1947, Indira Gandhi was the first woman to present the Budget (1970-71), and John Matthai presented the Republic's first Budget (1950).

st.1: Their interest rates are set every quarter by the Ministry of Finance.

x: All three statements are correct: the rates are set quarterly by the Ministry of Finance, the money goes to the NSSF in the Public Account, and the rates were unchanged for the 8th straight quarter on 31 March 2026.

st.2: Each bank branch is to lend to at least ten SC/ST and ten women borrowers.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: each branch is to lend to at least one SC/ST and one woman borrower. Statement 3 is wrong: the scheme covers manufacturing, services, trading and agri-allied activities.

st.2: Its 13 partial-withdrawal categories have been merged into 3 groups.

x: All three statements are correct: the 2026 Scheme replaces the 1952 Scheme under the Code on Social Security, merges 13 withdrawal categories into 3 groups, and keeps at least 25% of the balance.

st.1: It has been extended from 31 December 2024 to 31 March 2028.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the scheme runs to 31 March 2030. Statement 4 is wrong: coverage now extends to census towns and peri-urban areas.

st.3: A rural woman's earnings relative to a rural man's fell from 53% to 45%.

x: All three statements are correct: working women rose to about 201 million, the female WPR rose from 22% to 38%, and a rural woman's pay relative to a rural man's fell from 53% to 45%.

st.3: The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

x: All three statements are correct: Telangana was first in the PRAGATI review (best in 9 areas), Sahyog recorded 89.41% takedown success, and I4C is under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

st.3: The SDRF provides additional aid for disasters of severe nature, while the NDRF is the main State fund with Centre and State contributions.
st.1: In August 2026 the MHA added heatwave and lightning to the notified natural calamities, raising the list from 10 to 12.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the list rose from 12 to 14. Statement 2 is wrong: the addition followed the 16th, not the 15th, Finance Commission. Statement 3 is wrong: the NDRF gives additional aid for severe disasters and the SDRF is the main State fund.

st.2: Article 371(A), which protects Nagaland's customary law, remains intact in the FNTA areas.

x: All three statements are correct: FNTA funds follow population and area with MHA funding the set-up, Article 371(A) remains intact, and Manipur's Hill Areas Committee under Article 371(C) is a similar model.

st.1: The third round proposes leasing 11 AAI airports under PPP, in three bundles.
st.3: The model shifts from a per-passenger fee to revenue-sharing.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 11 airports are in five bundles. Statement 3 is wrong: the shift is from revenue-sharing to a per-passenger fee. Statement 4 is wrong: AERA's tariff cuts go up to 5%.

st.3: India will need 144 million new homes by 2070.

x: All three statements are correct: about 600 million Indians face high to extreme water stress, the urban population will near 1 billion by 2050, and 144 million new homes are needed by 2070.

st.3: Her total of 168 kg included a 76 kg snatch.

x: All three statements are correct: Juhita Guna is from Rajamahendravaram, won 69 kg youth gold at Ahmedabad in 2025, and lifted 76 kg snatch plus 92 kg clean and jerk for 168 kg.

st.3: The national e-Sanjeevani telemedicine service began in 2019.

x: All three statements are correct: AP's Sanjeevani project was piloted in Kuppam, ABDM was launched in 2021, and e-Sanjeevani began in 2019.

st.1: It cuts more than 800 regulations to fewer than 100 through executive orders alone.
st.4: CFMS, a digital tool used in it, stands for Centralised Fund Monitoring System.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the cut is through the Ordinance route. Statement 3 is wrong: colonial-era laws are removed, not retained. Statement 4 is wrong: CFMS is the Comprehensive Financial Management System.

st.2: It is an initiative for preventive healthcare.

x: All three statements are correct: Project Sanjeevani was launched at the Swasth Nari–Sashakt Parivar Abhiyan in Visakhapatnam, it is a preventive healthcare initiative, and its partners are the Gates Foundation and TCS.

st.1: AP ranked 1st in total pulse production in the country.
st.3: Production rose from 9.96 lakh tonnes to 25.71 lakh tonnes.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: AP ranked 1st in pulse production growth (+57.73%), not total output. Statement 3 is wrong: output rose to 15.71 lakh tonnes. Statement 4 is wrong: red gram was not the largest contributor.

st.1: P4 stands for Public–Private–Panchayat Partnership.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: P4 is the Public–Private–People Partnership. Statement 2 is wrong: the roadmap is the State's own, prepared with NITI Aayog inputs; NITI Aayog does not execute it.

st.1: Godavari water was sent to Uttarandhra through the Right Main Canal using pumps, though the dam is not finished.
st.4: The plan links the Godavari with the Penna.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the water went through the Left Main Canal. Statement 2 is wrong: the canal will irrigate 4 lakh acres; 9.23 lakh is the number of people to get drinking water. Statement 4 is wrong: the plan links the Godavari with the Vamsadhara.

st.3: It is the 29th airport in the Category-1 Immigration Check Post list.
st.1: It has a 4,800 m runway and an initial capacity of 6 million passengers a year.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the runway is 3,800 m. Statement 2 is wrong: it has a 5 MW solar plant. Statement 3 is wrong: it is the 39th airport in the Category-1 list.

st.4: The nodal department for the National Quantum Mission is the Department of Telecommunications.
st.3: AP's first Quantum Incubator is by IIT Tirupati at Medha Towers, Gannavaram.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 100% Grant-in-Aid comes from MeitY, not DST. Statement 3 is wrong: the incubator is by Chandigarh University. Statement 4 is wrong: the NQM's nodal department is the Department of Science and Technology.

st.3: The earlier NVIDIA MoU (2025) was for setting up the AI University itself.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the AI University is proposed with LG AI Research, not Samsung. Statement 3 is wrong: the NVIDIA MoU was for the AI ecosystem and compute, not the university.

st.2: The AP Sericulture Department won the Best Tableau award on Republic Day 2025.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the award was given at the CSB's 76th Foundation Day in Bengaluru, not Mysuru. Statement 2 is wrong: the Best Tableau award was on Independence Day 2025.
